newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA READY TO MAKE SEASON'S DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA READY TO MAKE SEASON'S DEBUT.

text.p: The Alberto Tomba show, delayed by the Italian skier's heavy fall before the season started, gets going at last on Tuesday.

The Italian Olympic and world championship hero, who kept everyone guessing for months about his eventual return, is ready to make his seasonal debut in Madonna di Campiglio -- where he also won his opening race of last season on his birthday.
To be precise, it has been 281 days since the double world champion and triple Olympic gold medallist last skied competitively and the sport desperately needs him.
His last race was on March 10, at the Norwegian resort of Lillehammer, where he was fourth in a slalom after winning the slalom and giant slalom world titles in February.

Since then there has been some agonising debate about whether or not he should retire, a decision now shelved until at least after the next world championships in the Italian resort of Sestriere and possibly to the end of the millenium.

Officially the Bolognese wants to use the Madonna di Campiglio slalom, on the Canalone Miramonti piste where he has won three World Cup slaloms before, to test out his ankle and wrist before the more arduous races ahead.

It will be the third men's slalom of the season and the first on European snow, with the others won by on-form Austrian Thomas Sykora in Park City and Norwegian Tom Stiansen, winning his first slalom, in the U.S. resort of Breckenridge.
Sykora leads the world slalom standings with 180 points, ahead of compatriot Thomas Stangassinger on 140.
The slalom specialists will be considerably fresher than others racing a super-G in Val d'Isere on Monday.
Tomba trained here last week and returned on Sunday night for final tests. The Italian was due to hold a news conference later in the afternoon to confirm he will race.

"Tomba, while still not being 100 percent fit, believes that the Campiglio slalom is an important test to put his preparations to the test after just three weeks of training," his publicity managers said in a statement on Sunday.
"He also wants to measure his preparations in a direct confrontation with the other slalom skiers."
Assuming, as everyone does, that Tomba will race then he will do so with a light cast on his right wrist.
One of the big reasons to believe that the Italian will be present is the fact that he celebrates his 30th birthday on Thursday and he rarely says no to a party.

Last year, after a disastrous piece of public relations at Alta Badia -- where he threw a glass trophy and a magnum of champagne at a photographer who had sold nude photos of him -- Tomba's fans rallied round with a cake at Madonna.
Tomba won the race and apologised to the photographer.
